Container.Name: Reolink-ONVIF-Proxy
Container.Overview:
Normalize malformed HTTP responses from affected Reolink ONVIF firmware so Frigate can use the camera's native PTZ service. Video, audio, and credentials remain direct between Frigate and the camera.
Example Frigate configuration:
cameras: camera_name: onvif: host: <unraid-server-address> port: 18890 user: <camera-username> password: <existing camera password> tls_insecure: true ignore_time_mismatch: true
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: reolink frigate onvif proxy camera pan tilt zoom ptz
Container.Requires: A Reolink camera with an ONVIF service reachable from Unraid. Install one instance per affected camera and assign each instance a unique host port.
Container.Changes: 2026-09-06: Initial release with DockerMan settings, health endpoint, response normalization, and optional client allowlist.

Config.Name: ONVIF proxy host port
Config.Description: Port Frigate uses to reach this proxy. Use a unique host port for each installed camera.

Config.Name: Camera name
Config.Description: Friendly label used in health output and logs.

Config.Name: Camera IP or hostname
Config.Description: LAN address of the Reolink camera.

Config.Name: Camera ONVIF port
Config.Description: Native ONVIF service port exposed by the camera. Reolink commonly uses 8000.

Config.Name: I/O timeout
Config.Description: Maximum upstream read or connection wait in seconds.

Config.Name: Allowed clients
Config.Description: Optional comma-separated IP/CIDR allowlist. Leave empty to accept any client that can reach this LAN port. Docker NAT may present clients as a 172.16.0.0/12 gateway address.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: Python log level: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, or ERROR.
